page: Microsoft Azure DC128eds_v6 is an enterprise-scale virtual machine within the DCEDV6 family, executed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor configuration delivering 128 dedicated vCPUs. With dedicated CPU allocation, computing threads avoid noisy-neighbor contention, providing steady execution for processor-heavy calculations and multi-threaded systems.

System memory is provisioned at 512.0 GB, which scales to exactly 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration aligns directly with standard general-purpose resource balances, preventing memory bottlenecks during high-concurrency operations. For persistent or caching I/O layers, the server bundles 7559 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, alongside architectural support for Azure Premium Storage. The high-capacity local NVMe tier delivers low-latency disk access directly on the host hypervisor.

The hardware specification contains no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network connectivity and external address spaces must be managed through standard cloud networking abstractions. From a resource perspective, bundling 128 dedicated cores with multi-terabyte local NVMe storage establishes strong qualitative cost efficiency for organizations looking to minimize external managed storage overhead for temporary or intermediate datasets.

Given its high physical resource allotment, the DC128eds_v6 is well suited for demanding relational databases, transactional data stores, distributed extract-transform-load (ETL) processing pipelines, search indexes, and large-scale web application serving platforms requiring significant local disk caching.
description: Microsoft Azure DC128eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel processor architecture and powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 512 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture is anchored by 7559 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, accommodating input/output intensive operations without external block volume latency. The hardware profile excludes dedicated graphics accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its density strictly toward high-throughput compute and storage tasks. This infrastructure envelope delivers balanced core density and substantial low-latency local storage, making the instance applicable for large-scale relational databases, enterprise transactional workloads, distributed data processing, and high-concurrency microservices.
